title: SeedSet
description:
Externally-produced candidate sequences injected into the initial population (ADR-0007, answering open question 6).

This interface does double duty, which is why it is worth building in Phase 1 rather than deferring: it is both the migration path for existing LinearDesign/CDSfold/CodonTransformer users AND the mechanism by which the benchmark harness places a competitor's output on DNA Design Suite's own objective axes for the head-to-head comparisons required by BRIEF-2.5.

ACCEPTANCE IS STRICT AND EXPLAINED. A seed is admitted only if it translates to exactly the target protein under the target translation table. A seed that fails is reported with a positional diff, never silently dropped - a user who pastes the wrong file must be told which residue disagrees.

target_protein_digest.description: sha256 over the UTF-8 bytes of `target_protein`. A bare residue string rather than a document, so this is the one digest in the schemas taken over raw bytes; every other digest is over an RFC 8785 canonical document.

digest.description: Digest of the CodonSequence DOCUMENT for this seed (sequence.schema.json), not of the `cds` string. Seeds are quoted without flanks, so the document is the one built from `cds` under `translation_table` with no flanking context. Using the document digest is what makes a seed comparable with a Pareto-front candidate and with `observation.as_built_digest`.

parameters.description: e.g. LinearDesign's lambda. Recorded because a competitor's point on the MFE/CAI trade-off curve is meaningless without the trade-off parameter that produced it.

reported_metrics.description: Metrics as reported by the originating tool (e.g. its own CAI and MFE). Kept separately from DNA Design Suite's own recomputation so that a discrepancy is visible rather than hidden - different tools use different CAI reference sets.

repaired.description: Whether constraint repair was applied before injection. A seed from a tool that does not know about the user's assembly standard will usually need it.

max_fraction_of_population.description: Capped because a population dominated by near-identical seeds from one tool collapses diversity in the first few generations and the search never explores.

also_inject_mutated_copies.description: Injecting a seed plus a few perturbed copies gives the crossover operator material to work with immediately.

protect_for_generations.description: Elitism grace period for seeds. Default 0: a seed that cannot survive on merit should not be protected.
